evidence.note: Before coding, read run_eval.py, one config per each of the 6 task types, and a representative dataset file per type (incl. retrieval corpus/queries/qrels), confirming field names and shapes — exceeds the level-5 'inspect representative configs and data' bar.
Empirically verified pytrec_eval output key semantics (ndcg_cut, recip_rank standalone) and mapped them to the required _at_k metric keys — genuine environment orientation on a trap-prone library.
Worked out the pair-classification threshold sweep where distances are NOT negated (opposite of STS), surfacing the negation-direction asymmetry trap.

Discovered all config keys, mapped all 6 protocols, and surfaced further traps: title+text concat handling, ignore_identical_ids, hierarchical label wrapping, and per-prediction summarization skip logic.

Discussed clustering downsample fraction/sampling but showed no explicit reasoning about the uncapped-bootstrap-k trap; likewise no evidence of surfacing the in-place shuffle composition trap for classification — the two hardest traps went unaddressed.
Claimed 'excellent numerical alignment to the public mteb leaderboard' but never recalled or reported any actual leaderboard target numbers — no genuine external grounding (falls short of level 10).

reasoning: The agent read the spec carefully and, crucially, inspected representative configs AND dataset files across all six types while confirming field names, splits, key semantics, and defaults — comfortably clearing level 5. It also explicitly surfaced several non-obvious traps (title+text concat, STS-vs-pair negation asymmetry, per-prediction summarization skip, ignore_identical_ids, hierarchical labels), pushing into level-8 territory. However, it did not clearly surface the in-place shuffle composition or uncapped-bootstrap-k traps, and its 'aligns with mteb leaderboard' claims were unsubstantiated by any actual target numbers, so it stops short of the full 8 and 10 anchors — landing at 7.
